appraisal_events.evidence: « j’affectais une froideur dont Andrée fut peut-être moins dupe que moi de sa crédulité apparente » ; « Pourquoi donc lui échappa-t-il […] : “J’ai justement vu la tante à Albertine” ? » ; « — Je n’en ai jamais douté un seul instant », s’écria Andrée d’un ton amer » ; « elles étaient les débris informes et reconstituables de cette pensée que j’avais fait exploser, en la heurtant, malgré Andrée »
appraisal_events.explanation: The whole apparatus of feints the narrator builds — pretending to prefer Andrée, slandering Mme Bontemps, using Elstir as a secret intermediary — is shown to be transparent: Andrée reads him at the second degree and says so bitterly, and the retrospective narrator endorses the exposure by explaining how his own words betrayed him. His scheming also yields nothing (« qui passaient sans rien m’apporter de décisif »).

appraisal_events.evidence: « Il est probable qu’au contraire elle ne croyait pas à la première ni ne souhaitait la seconde » ; « Et probablement n’en était-elle pas heureuse » ; « me répondit Andrée d’un air mécontent […] Moi, qu’est-ce que vous voulez que cela me fasse que vous la voyiez ou non ? Cela m’est bien égal. »
appraisal_events.explanation: The second movement turns Andrée's own dissimulation inside out: her professed wish for the narrator's union with Albertine is declared insincere, her bitterness and discontented look are noted, and her closing protest of indifference is placed so as to read as jealousy she cannot conceal.

status_effects.explanation: His carefully managed indifference and calculated malice about Mme Bontemps fail as speech acts: Andrée is not deceived and throws his own pretence back at him.
He gains no leverage from the manoeuvre: the awaited days collapse « comme des vagues » without anything decisive, and he ends the passage being told Albertine will not want to see him.
She holds the discerning position: the « justement » and « Je n’en ai jamais douté un seul instant » show she has decoded the narrator's design while he believed himself opaque.
Her own feigned indifference is presented as unhappy and jealous, so her insight costs her the composure it displays.

ambiguities: The passage cuts both ways for Andrée: the same scene that credits her with penetrating the narrator's design also exposes her insincerity and jealousy. This is annotated as two distinct movements (E1 rhetorical gain, E2 emotional loss) rather than collapsed into a single verdict, because the text stages her lucidity and her discomfiture in separate stretches.

Andrée's superiority rests entirely on the narrator's own conjecture — « peut-être moins dupe », « Il est probable », « probablement » — so her decoding of his intentions is inferred rather than shown. E1 is nevertheless read as an endorsed diminishment of the narrator because her bitter « Je n’en ai jamais douté un seul instant » is direct speech that the narrator concedes he provoked « malgré Andrée ».
